summary: DESIGN stage fan-out: independent architects each propose an approach from a distinct angle AND the guardrail rules it would add, then a judge scores them against the code rails and synthesizes the winner. Produces the chosen approach and the rules the contract must carry.
logs: 3 approaches proposed; judging against the code rails

keySteps: Add analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/WrittenTypeScanner.cs: internal static class with Register(CompilationStartAnalysisContext, Action<SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext,INamedTypeSymbol>) and RegisterForAssembly(CompilationStartAnalysisContext, string, Action<SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext,INamedTypeSymbol>), registering SyntaxKind.IdentifierName and SyntaxKind.GenericName, dispatching through context.SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo(context.Node, context.CancellationToken).Symbol is INamedTypeSymbol.
Amend contract.md's Surfaces list to add WrittenTypeScanner.cs beside DeclaredTypeScanner.cs (mechanical, since a second file was already approved and only its name was open).

RULE-PHASE builds EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer (AG0041) calling WrittenTypeScanner.RegisterForAssembly twice (guard, AgentGuard.TestHelpers), with its own internal-Engine-type predicate and its own single receiver-of-Create()-invocation exemption (a small syntax parent-walk local to that file, not extracted, since it has exactly one consumer).

RULE-PHASE extends OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzer (AG0023) and OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzer (AG0029) with one WrittenTypeScanner.RegisterForAssembly(context, EngineAssembly.Name, inspect) call each on their Engine gate only, reusing each rule's existing assembly-scope test and WellKnownType.IsInAssembly for its own door type, combined with the new CompositionPoint method-level caller check.

RULE-PHASE writes the fixture battery from contract Acceptance 9-12 and 20-22 — one fixture per listed position (typeof, nameof, cast, is-pattern, switch pattern, generic type argument, generic constraint, base list, attribute argument, using alias, array element, pointer element, plain declaration) — which empirically proves the leaf-registration coverage claim rather than resting on the structural argument alone.

RULE-PHASE resolves the one open verification item during fixture-writing: confirm GetSymbolInfo on a used (not declared) using-alias name resolves through to the aliased type directly; if it instead yields an IAliasSymbol, add one unwrap (Symbol is IAliasSymbol alias ? alias.Target as INamedTypeSymbol : ...) inside WrittenTypeScanner.Dispatch itself, since that is a resolution-correctness detail of the scanner, not rule policy.

rulesToAdd.rule: New self-hosting analyzer (name/ID assigned at RULE-PHASE, category AgentGuard.Architecture, Warning severity matching every existing rule): ban a direct call to SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo/GetTypeInfo/GetAliasInfo anywhere in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/*.cs except inside a small named allowlist of owner files (WrittenTypeScanner.cs; the three pre-existing sites ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer.cs, AttributeIdentity.cs, NoOsBranchingOutsideCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs). Gated to the AgentGuard.Analyzers compilation itself.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A future contributor hand-rolls a second written-name (or written-anything) resolution inline inside a new or edited rule instead of calling WrittenTypeScanner, quietly recreating the 'two lenses have exactly one owner' violation that contract Acceptance 23 currently catches only by a human 'read every registration' pass. This turns that manual check into a wired, build-breaking one, matching rails-solid-code rule 6 (gate wired in, not remembered) instead of leaving it as something REFUTE has to remember to re-verify by hand every time a rule touches a type name.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: RegisterSyntaxNodeAction-based Roslyn analyzer over the analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers project's own source, in the same self-hosting style as AG0018 (TestHelpersOnlyInTestsAnalyzer) already applies to that project's own reference graph. Flagged here as a recommendation for the DESIGN judge/CONTRACT to accept or defer, not built unilaterally, since it is a new category of guardrail (linting the analyzer project's own code) adjacent to but outside this contract's stated scope of 'the analyzer rules... that keep the resulting access narrow' in src/.

risks: Using-alias resolution is unverified against live Roslyn behavior: whether GetSymbolInfo on a USE of a using-alias name (not its declaration) already unwraps to the aliased type directly, or returns an IAliasSymbol requiring an explicit .Target unwrap inside Dispatch. Contained and directly testable by the contract's own required using-alias fixture (Acceptance 9); at worst a few-line addition to WrittenTypeScanner.Dispatch, not a design change.

WrittenTypeScanner and DeclaredTypeScanner will both fire on an ordinary non-var declaration of a guarded type (e.g. a field explicitly typed SystemServices) -- one hit from each lens on the same line. This is deliberate and already authorized by contract Acceptance 11 ('No AG0041 test uses Assert.Single on an input that can trip both lenses'); flagging it so RULE-PHASE's fixtures assert the correct multi-diagnostic count instead of treating the overlap as a bug to suppress.

Registering on SyntaxKind.IdentifierName/GenericName visits every identifier and generic name in the gated compilation, not just type positions -- broader than AG0007's four narrow registrations. Bounded in practice: AG0041 gates to two small compilations (guard, AgentGuard.TestHelpers) and AG0023/AG0029's Engine gate to one (AgentGuard.Engine), and RawPrimitiveOnlyInOwnerAnalyzer (AG0011) already registers fully unfiltered across every compilation in this same analyzer suite, so this is within the project's existing performance envelope, not a new category of cost.

The proposed self-hosting 'one owner of GetSymbolInfo' rule (see rulesToAdd) is a genuinely new kind of guardrail -- it lints the analyzer project's own code, which nothing in this codebase does today -- and sits adjacent to but outside this contract's named scope. Surfaced as a recommendation, not assumed into the approach, so it does not silently expand what this run builds.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the new written-name lens should be built as a fresh, self-contained implementation or extracted/reused from existing primitives.
autoResolved.resolution: Extract into one shared internal static class that reuses WellKnownType.IsInAssembly for identity and mirrors MemberUseScanner's Register/RegisterForAssembly gate-then-scan shape verbatim, rather than reimplementing identity matching or compilation gating inline in each of AG0041/AG0023/AG0029.
autoResolved.principle: rails-dry-code rule 8 (reuse a tested primitive behind one deliberate owner, never hand-reimplement it) and rule 1 (the prior-art ledger already ruled 'extract' for this capability)
autoResolved.evidence: ground-ledger.json capability 'type-reference-lens' verdict: decision='extract', citing ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer.cs and ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer.cs as the two existing half-owners neither of which is copied wholesale.

autoResolved.choice: Where the SystemServices-as-Create()-receiver exemption and the door-type-plus-caller-site exemption should live: inside the shared scanner, or inside each consuming rule.
autoResolved.resolution: The scanner reports only 'this node names a type X' and takes no position on whether X is permitted here; every exemption (the receiver-of-Create() check for AG0041, the door-type-plus-caller-site check for AG0023/AG0029) is decided entirely inside the consuming rule's own Inspect callback.
autoResolved.principle: feedback-abstraction-mirrors-primitive-not-policy.md (user's standing working rule): 'a boundary wrapper faithfully mirrors the BCL/OS surface (own + mockable); domain policy (fail-closed) lives at the CALL SITE, never baked into the wrapper'
autoResolved.evidence: MemberUseScanner.cs:43-98 already follows this exact split today -- Register/Dispatch resolve the member use and hand it to the caller's inspect delegate; every door/permission decision (AG0023's CrossPlatformAdapters check, AG0029's PlatformServices check) lives in each analyzer's own Inspect, not in MemberUseScanner itself.

autoResolved.choice: Whether nested type-name positions (inside a generic argument, array element, pointer target, or qualified/aliased name) need a manual recursive walk (TypeTree.Any) over the resolved symbol, or are already reached by registering on the leaf syntax kinds.
autoResolved.resolution: No recursive walk is added. Registering on SyntaxKind.IdentifierName and SyntaxKind.GenericName alone reaches every nested position, because Roslyn's syntax tree already represents each nested type-name occurrence as its own independently-visited leaf node (RegisterSyntaxNodeAction visits every node of a given kind regardless of nesting depth); adding TypeTree.Any on top would duplicate coverage the leaf registration already provides.
autoResolved.principle: rails-real-work rule 8 (take the correct approach, not the cheaper one that was handed to you, and report it) combined with rails-solid-code rule 7 (no premature/redundant machinery beyond the known need)
autoResolved.evidence: Traced concretely against SystemServices.Create()'s live body (src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:90-91): 'CrossPlatformAdapters' and 'PlatformServices' each resolve correctly as independent leaf IdentifierNameSyntax nodes without any symbol-level recursion; confirmed no existing analyzer registers this way today (ground-facts.json analyzer-fence claim, grep for SyntaxKind.IdentifierName|GenericName|QualifiedName|TypeOfExpression|NameOf across analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/*.cs returns zero hits).

keySteps: Verify empirically (not by memory of the grammar) which syntax kinds every contract-named position bottoms out in: compiled and ran a throwaway Roslyn probe against Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.14.0 covering typeof, both forms of nameof, a cast, as, is-pattern, case-pattern, a generic argument, a generic constraint, a base-list entry, an attribute argument, a using alias, an array element, a pointer element, and every declaration position — confirmed all resolve through IdentifierName/GenericName/QualifiedName/AliasQualifiedName.

Verify the double-report risk and its fix empirically: confirmed GetSymbolInfo on a QualifiedNameSyntax and on its own nested trailing IdentifierName resolve to the identical symbol, then confirmed a parent-based skip rule (skip a QualifiedName's Left/Right or an AliasQualifiedName's Name) collapses an arbitrarily deep qualified/aliased chain — including one nested inside a generic type argument nested inside another qualified name — to exactly one visit, with zero loss of the positions that must still fire independently.

Verify the exact API surface by reflection rather than assumption: SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo(SyntaxNode, CancellationToken) resolves via Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ModelExtensions (not the C#-specific ExpressionSyntax-only overloads); RegisterSyntaxNodeAction has an ImmutableArray<SyntaxKind> overload matching MemberUseScanner's existing pattern; SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext.ContainingSymbol exists in the same ISymbol shape as OperationAnalysisContext.ContainingSymbol, so the already-approved CompositionPoint caller-site check needs no adaptation.
Add analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/WrittenNameScanner.cs with the Register/RegisterForAssembly surface shown, mirroring MemberUseScanner's calling convention exactly.

Wire AG0041 to call WrittenNameScanner.RegisterForAssembly twice (guard, AgentGuard.TestHelpers); wire AG0023's and AG0029's Engine gates to call it once each (AgentGuard.Engine) beside their existing MemberUseScanner registration — all three are RULE-PHASE's work, not built in this design pass.
Leave DeclaredTypeScanner as the unchanged carried-type half exactly as Tim already decided; this file adds no dependency on it and reopens no part of the split.
Add the proposed structural regression test (see Rules to add) so the single-owner property this design establishes is enforced by the build going forward, not only true on the day this lands.
risks: The chain-deduplication skip rule (IsPartOfEnclosingName) is load-bearing, not cosmetic: omitting it silently doubles the diagnostic count for every qualified reference (e.g. AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices used as a field type), which would break the exact-count assertions Acceptance 9-11 and 20-21 require across all three consumers. TDD/RULE-PHASE must carry this logic forward unmodified, not simplify it away as 'just resolve every name node'.

The written-name lens and DeclaredTypeScanner (the carried-type lens) will both independently fire on an ordinary declaration position (a field/property/parameter/local typed as the banned type) — this is deliberate, contract-blessed overlap ('no cross-lens deduplication is built'), not a defect, but it means the TDD author must compute exact expected counts per fixture rather than assume one diagnostic per statement; Acceptance 11 already anticipates this ('No AG0041 test uses Assert.Single on an input that can trip both lenses').

nameof's qualified form (nameof(AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices)) parses as a nested MemberAccessExpressionSyntax chain of plain IdentifierNames (expression grammar), not QualifiedNameSyntax (type grammar) — verified empirically. A reviewer who assumes nameof's dotted form behaves like a cast's dotted form would misjudge this lens's coverage; it is in fact still fully covered, just via the ordinary per-segment IdentifierName path rather than the QualifiedName path.

A name inside an XML doc-comment <see cref="..."/> is not visited (RegisterSyntaxNodeAction does not descend into structured trivia by default). This is not a gap against the contract, which never names a cref among its required positions, but it should be stated explicitly so it is not later mistaken for an overlooked case.

AG0007 (ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer) has the identical 'enumerated syntax-kind list, next position silently escapes' gap this design fixes for AG0041/AG0023/AG0029 — but for a different type-set (contract-implementation classes, not Engine-internal/CrossPlatform-core/per-OS types) and it is not named anywhere in this contract's Decisions, Surfaces, or Acceptance. Migrating AG0007 onto WrittenNameScanner would be a genuine improvement but is out of this contract's scope; worth a follow-up GitHub issue rather than folding into this run.

rulesToAdd.rule: A structural regression test (xUnit, not a Roslyn DiagnosticAnalyzer) in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests, reusing the existing RepositoryFiles helper and following the same kind as the existing OsSpecificFileNotCrossCompiledTests: scan every .cs file under analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/ for a RegisterSyntaxNodeAction call naming SyntaxKind.IdentifierName, GenericName, QualifiedName, or AliasQualifiedName, and assert the only file where any appears is WrittenNameScanner.cs; separately assert the four declared-type registrations (RegisterSymbolAction(SymbolKind.Field/Property/Method) plus RegisterOperationAction(..., OperationKind.VariableDeclarator) paired with a TypeTree/leaf-test walk) appear only in DeclaredTypeScanner.cs.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A later analyzer author (human or AI, on a future issue) needs a fourth consumer for either lens and, instead of calling the one existing owner, hand-registers a fresh, narrower syntax-kind list (reintroducing AG0007's exact 'next position silently escapes' gap) or copy-pastes the resolution logic into a new file — the precise DRY rail-4 failure ('reuse'/'extract' ruled but a fresh copy written anyway) and SOLID rail-5 failure (the fix does not generalize to the next case). Nothing catches this today at build time, because the analyzer project does not apply its own diagnostics to itself (AgentGuardIsAnalyzerProject excludes it from the Directory.Build.props analyzer-reference wiring), so only a test-level structural check closes the gap.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: xUnit structural test (file/text scan via the existing RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot + Directory.EnumerateFiles), not a Roslyn DiagnosticAnalyzer — the same category as the already-shipped OsSpecificFileNotCrossCompiledTests, wired into the normal `make test` run rather than a separate mechanism.

autoResolved.choice: Whether WrittenNameScanner exposes both an ungated Register and a gated RegisterForAssembly, mirroring MemberUseScanner's two-tier surface, or only the gated form the three known consumers actually use.
autoResolved.resolution: Expose both, mirroring MemberUseScanner.cs's existing Register/RegisterForAssembly pair exactly; RegisterForAssembly already has to call an ungated scan internally, so exposing that scan costs one accessibility keyword and keeps the calling convention identical across sibling scanners.
autoResolved.principle: rails-decisions: "The agent's decisions — just do it, don't ask. Local work with no blast radius: a loop, a helper's internals, a private name...cheaply changed later with no ripple."
autoResolved.evidence: analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/MemberUseScanner.cs:43 (Register) and :61-73 (RegisterForAssembly, which calls Register internally); GuardedConstructionAnalyzer.cs:119 already consumes the bare Register form directly, proving both tiers of the sibling scanner see real, independent use today.

autoResolved.choice: Whether WrittenNameScanner needs its own message-formatting helper (a Describe(ISymbol), analogous to MemberUseScanner.Describe(member, type)).
autoResolved.resolution: No. MemberUseScanner.Describe exists only because that scanner splits one reference into two separate values (member + declaring type) that need combining into 'Type.Member' text; WrittenNameScanner hands back one resolved ISymbol, and symbol.ToDisplayString() is the whole of what a caller needs, so a wrapper would be a speculative addition with no real complexity behind it.
autoResolved.principle: rails-solid-code rail 7: a speculative escape hatch/extension point built "for later" with no real, approved need is a Violation; "Fix: ...delete the speculative hatch."
autoResolved.evidence: analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/MemberUseScanner.cs:82-87 (Describe combines member+type because Resolve() at :108-120 splits one IOperation into that pair); no contract Acceptance criterion (9-11, 20-21) asks for formatted display text, only for the correct diagnostic to be reported.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the gate check inside RegisterForAssembly should call the existing OwnerClass.InAssembly factory or re-inline its own string.Equals(context.Compilation.AssemblyName, assemblyName, StringComparison.Ordinal) check the way MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly does today.
autoResolved.resolution: Call the existing OwnerClass.InAssembly(assemblyName) factory. It is already the one owner of exactly this predicate; deriving a third copy inside a brand-new file would itself be the DRY violation this whole design exists to prevent, not something to reproduce.
autoResolved.principle: rails-dry-code rail 8 ("default to reusing a tested...primitive...the one-owner rule is a forcing function to pick the deliberate owner, never a bar to reuse") and rails-decisions' Exception-to-a-settled-rule section ("Reusing a tested...primitive by routing it through its one deliberate owner...is applying the rule, not escaping it").
autoResolved.evidence: analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/OwnerClass.cs:107-110 (InAssembly(string) already returns Func<Compilation,bool> testing compilation.AssemblyName == ownerAssemblyName); MemberUseScanner.cs:67's inline copy of the same predicate predates and is outside this work's scope to fix, so it is left untouched rather than joined by a third copy.

autoResolved.choice: Whether WrittenNameScanner should descend into structured trivia to also resolve a name inside an XML doc-comment <see cref="..."/>.
autoResolved.resolution: No. RegisterSyntaxNodeAction does not visit structured trivia by default, and the contract's own required-position list never names a doc-comment cref, so there is nothing approved to opt into.
autoResolved.principle: rails-real-work rail 3 ("Design for all N inputs...the objective actually requires") read against rails-decisions' boundary test — the objective is the contract's own named position list; covering a position the contract never asked for is unrequested scope, not thoroughness.
autoResolved.evidence: contract.md lines 79 and 83 (AG0041's exception and coverage text) and line 98 (AG0023/29's coverage text) enumerate the required positions exhaustively without a cref or any other doc-comment construct.

autoResolved.choice: The private name and internal shape of the chain-deduplication check (IsPartOfEnclosingName) inside Dispatch.
autoResolved.resolution: A private static predicate pattern-matching on QualifiedNameSyntax.Left/.Right and AliasQualifiedNameSyntax.Name, verified empirically to collapse an arbitrarily deep qualified/aliased chain to exactly one visit at its outermost node while leaving every independently-nested name (a generic argument, an array element) visited on its own.
autoResolved.principle: rails-decisions: "How a named thing is internally coded (a loop, a helper, a name) is implementation, not a decision, and needs no sign-off."
autoResolved.evidence: Empirical probe (compiled and run via dotnet against Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.14.0, the version this repo already restores) confirmed GetSymbolInfo on a QualifiedNameSyntax and on its own trailing IdentifierName resolve to the identical NamedType symbol, and confirmed the skip rule reduces a nested AgentGuard.Engine.SomeGeneric<AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices> field type to exactly one match (the inner type argument) with zero loss of coverage.

keySteps: Read AG0007 (ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer.cs) directly — confirmed it is the narrowing risk the contract warns against: 4 hand-picked SyntaxKinds, not a general lens.

Read MemberUseScanner.cs, TypeTree.cs, CompositionPoint.cs, WellKnownType.cs, PlatformFactory.cs, and both existing OneDoor analyzers to ground the established scanner idiom (gate-then-dispatch, unfiltered callback, caller owns policy) that WrittenNameScanner must match.

Read the live SystemServices.cs (src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:86-107) to verify, against real code, that CrossPlatformAdapters is both a written name and a carried type while PlatformServices is written-name-only — the exact fact the AG0029 ruling turns on.
Located and read the existing 'Rule N of the ruleset (a test, not a Roslyn analyzer)' precedent (RepositoryFiles.cs + 3 consuming test classes) as the reuse owner for the proposed guardrail tests.

Designed WrittenNameScanner.cs: register on SyntaxKind.IdentifierName + SyntaxKind.GenericName only (exhaustive by construction), syntax-based not operation-based, no QualifiedName/MemberAccessExpression registration (avoids duplicate reports, verified against the live qualified-call shape).
Defined the exact Register/RegisterForAssembly public surface, deliberately mirroring MemberUseScanner's shape so the three consuming rules compose both lenses identically.
Ruled that AG0029's carried-type exemption needs zero production case and must be proven by a synthetic fixture only, never by editing Create().
Proposed 4 structural single-owner guardrail tests plus 1 fixture-coverage addition (generic-named guarded symbol) closing a gap the literal Acceptance-9 text doesn't yet force.
This file name and surface, and the AG0029 ruling, go to Tim for approval per contract.md's explicit requirement before RULE-PHASE builds anything against them.

rulesToAdd.rule: written-name-lens-single-owner: a structural test (suggested: AnalyzerLensSingleOwnerTests.cs, reusing RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot()/IsUnderIntermediateOutput exactly as OsSpecificFileNotCrossCompiledTests does) fails if any .cs file under analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers OTHER than WrittenNameScanner.cs contains a RegisterSyntaxNodeAction call naming SyntaxKind.IdentifierName or SyntaxKind.GenericName. Include a planted-regression fixture (a second file with such a call) proving the check has teeth, matching the established idiom.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A rule author under time pressure inlines 'just this one more SyntaxKind check' directly inside AG0023/AG0029/AG0041's own Initialize instead of calling WrittenNameScanner, silently creating a second, narrower, divergent written-name implementation the other two rules don't share — the exact 'second inline implementation not greppable' and 'three consuming rules drift their own coverage' failure the brief names.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: contract-directed test rule (xunit structural/source-inspection test, not a compiled Roslyn DiagnosticAnalyzer — nothing in this repo self-hosts an analyzer against analyzers/ itself)

rulesToAdd.rule: carried-type-lens-single-owner: the same structural-test class fails if any .cs file other than DeclaredTypeScanner.cs (and its own test file) calls TypeTree.Any(...). Symmetric guardrail for the other lens, with its own planted-regression fixture.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: The same inline-reimplementation corner-cut, applied to the carried-type half instead of the written-name half — closes the gap for 'either lens', not just the one this stage was asked to design.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: contract-directed test rule (same file/class as the written-name single-owner test)

rulesToAdd.rule: type-reference-extension-stays-off-boundaries-gate: a structural test asserts that within OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs and OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzer.cs, every WrittenNameScanner/DeclaredTypeScanner registration call names EngineAssembly.Name (never BoundaryAssembly.Name), and that the existing MemberUseScanner Boundaries-gate call is never re-pointed to EngineAssembly.Name.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A copy-paste of the new Engine-gate registration block onto the existing Boundaries-gate block (or vice versa) silently wires the type-reference extension onto the Boundaries gate — directly violating the contract's 'Do not add the type-reference coverage to either rule's Boundaries gate.' This is a stronger, structural guarantee than Acceptance 22's behavioral fixture, which could pass by coincidence if the fixture set doesn't happen to probe the newly-added position against a Boundaries compilation.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: contract-directed test rule (same file/class as above)

rulesToAdd.rule: caller-site-test-single-owner: a structural test fails if AG0040/AG0041/AG0023/AG0029's own source files contain a hand-rolled 'is this symbol enclosed by SystemServices.Create()' check (a local walk over ContainingType/ContainingSymbol comparing against a method named Create) instead of calling CompositionPoint's contracted method-level check.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: The same single-owner risk applied to the third piece of shared logic these four rules need (the caller-site test), which contract.md already assigns to CompositionPoint — closes the loop so a rule author can't reinvent 'am I inside Create()' locally under the same time pressure that would produce a second lens implementation.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: contract-directed test rule (same file/class as above)

rulesToAdd.rule: AG0041's fixture set (Acceptance 9) should add one case beyond its literal text: an internal Engine type that is itself declared generic (e.g. internal sealed class InternalCache<T>), referenced with type arguments in a written-name position that is not also a DeclaredTypeScanner position (e.g. a cast: (InternalCache<int>)obj, or a base-list entry). Assert it is reported.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: SyntaxKind.GenericName is required in WrittenNameScanner's registered kind set — omitting it (e.g. a later 'simplification' that keeps only IdentifierName) would silently miss every internal Engine type that happens to be generic, in every position DeclaredTypeScanner doesn't independently cover. The literal Acceptance-9 list ('a generic type argument' means the guarded type used AS an argument, e.g. List<Guarded>, which is IdentifierName-only) does not force a fixture that would catch this specific regression, so without this addition the gap is invisible to the acceptance-mandated tests even though my design correctly handles it today.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: TDD acceptance-fixture addition to EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs (not a new analyzer or structural test — a required test case)

risks: The exemption's approved wording ('SystemServices... named as the receiver of an invocation of its static Create method') literally describes a receiver-present syntax shape. A hypothetical using-static AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices; plus a bare Create() call resolves to the identical SystemServices.Create method symbol but has no 'SystemServices named as receiver' at that call site — so a syntax-shape-keyed exemption test could misclassify it (either direction, depending on implementation), while a semantically-keyed test (via CompositionPoint/OneDoorRule's resolved-symbol identity, applied at the invocation/target-method level) would not. Neither current production call site uses using-static, so nothing in this contract's acceptance criteria exercises this today; flagging for RULE-PHASE to implement the exemption test semantically, matching how PlatformFactory.Is already tests resolved identity rather than syntax shape, since I have no authority to reinterpret the contract's already-approved exemption wording myself.

DeclaredTypeScanner's own exact public surface is Tim's already-decided territory, not mine to pin down here. The single-owner guardrails above (and the 'compose both lenses identically' property the illustrative example relies on) work best if RULE-PHASE keeps DeclaredTypeScanner's Register/RegisterForAssembly shape dispatch-symmetric to WrittenNameScanner's (CompilationStartAnalysisContext + assembly-name gate + unfiltered per-occurrence Action callback) rather than a differently-shaped API — recommended, not mandated, since it's outside this angle's charter.

GROUND flagged a separate, still-open RULE-PHASE decision: whether SharedAnalyzerSources.cs carries one shared fake-AgentGuard.Engine fixture constant or two differently-shaped ones (a subject-compilation shape for AG0040/23/29's Engine gate vs. a reference-compilation shape for AG0041). My design doesn't depend on which way that resolves, but it's adjacent enough to this file's consumers that it's worth keeping visible rather than letting it get lost between this stage and RULE-PHASE.

The generic-named-guarded-symbol fixture gap (rulesToAdd #5) is real but easy to lose: it's a gap in the contract's literal Acceptance-9 text, not something any existing acceptance criterion already forces. If this DESIGN record doesn't survive into the contract or into TDD's actual fixture set, the coverage gap it closes goes back to being invisible.

autoResolved.choice: Should WrittenNameScanner's dispatch mechanism be a fresh, bespoke registration pattern, or mirror MemberUseScanner's existing Register/RegisterForAssembly shape (compilation-start registration, an assembly-name gate, an unfiltered per-occurrence callback that hands the caller everything and lets the caller own all filtering/diagnostics)?
autoResolved.resolution: Mirror MemberUseScanner's shape exactly: Register/RegisterForAssembly, unfiltered Action<...> callback, caller owns all policy and reporting.
autoResolved.principle: best-practices-guide 2c (mirror the surface of the thing you wrap so callers meet a familiar surface and no vocabulary is invented) + rails-solid-code rail 4 (no unjustified second path — extend the existing path's shape rather than inventing a divergent one without a stated reason)
autoResolved.evidence: MemberUseScanner.cs:43-73 — the exact Register/RegisterForAssembly shape already in production and already used identically by AG0023 and AG0029 today. TypeTree.cs:25 shows a genuinely different shape (predicate-in, bool-out) used for a genuinely different job (single-root containment, not compilation-wide dispatch), confirming the dispatch-shape choice tracks the job rather than being a style preference.

autoResolved.choice: Should WrittenNameScanner also register on SyntaxKind.QualifiedName / MemberAccessExpression to directly catch a dotted/qualified reference 'as a whole', or register only on the two leaf SimpleNameSyntax kinds (IdentifierName, GenericName) and rely on each nested leaf resolving independently?
autoResolved.resolution: Leaf kinds only. No QualifiedName/MemberAccessExpression registration.
autoResolved.principle: rails-dry-code rail 6 (no duplicated block/logic — here, duplicate diagnostics from one written occurrence)
autoResolved.evidence: Verified against the live SystemServices.Create() body (src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:90-91): global::AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.PlatformServices.Create() parses with 'PlatformServices' as its own IdentifierNameSyntax leaf inside the nested MemberAccessExpressionSyntax chain; registering on IdentifierName alone already visits and resolves that leaf, so an additional registration on the enclosing MemberAccessExpressionSyntax would report the identical symbol from the identical statement a second time.

autoResolved.choice: Should the written-name lens register via RegisterOperationAction (IOperation, the shape MemberUseScanner already uses) or RegisterSyntaxNodeAction (syntax)?
autoResolved.resolution: Syntax-based (RegisterSyntaxNodeAction on IdentifierName/GenericName), not operation-based.
autoResolved.principle: rails-real-work rail 1 (cover the whole input set the objective names, not the easy/deterministic subset) — operation-based registration is structurally incapable of covering the whole set the contract names.
autoResolved.evidence: A generic constraint (where T : Foo), a base-list entry, and an attribute-argument type reference are declaration-time constructs with no IOperation representation at all in Roslyn's operation tree — confirmed against the existing IOperation-kind list MemberUseScanner registers (Invocation, ObjectCreation, PropertyReference, FieldReference, MethodReference; MemberUseScanner.cs:29-34), none of which fire for a non-executable declaration position.

autoResolved.choice: Should the registered kind set be {IdentifierName} alone, or {IdentifierName, GenericName}?

verdict.why:
Risk-first is the only candidate that is right on the mechanism, right on the callback type, and right on the file name at the same time — and it is the only one that produced a code-verified ruling on a gap none of the others saw. I verified its central claims against live Roslyn 4.14.0 (the pinned version) with a probe over all eleven contract-named positions, and against the live tree.

MECHANISM. Risk-first and simplest both register only the two concrete SimpleNameSyntax kinds (IdentifierName, GenericName); most-general registers four (adding QualifiedName, AliasQualifiedName) and then needs an IsPartOfEnclosingName skip rule to stop double-reporting. The probe settles it against most-general: leaf-only produced 32 hits, four-kinds-plus-skip produced 31, and the one hit the skip rule LOSES is real — in `N.Outer.Inner`, leaf-only catches both `N.Outer` and `N.Outer.Inner`, the skip rule catches only the inner. Leaf-only is a strict superset. Most-general's extra machinery adds zero coverage, costs a dedup pass, and removes a catch from a fail-closed guard. Its own "verified empirically" duplicate is self-inflicted: the duplicate only exists because it registered QualifiedName.

CALLBACK TYPE. Simplest hands back `INamedTypeSymbol`. The probe kills it: an attribute's own name node resolves through `GetSymbolInfo` to the attribute CONSTRUCTOR (`[N.GuardedAttr]` → `Method:N.GuardedAttr.GuardedAttr()`), not the type — so an internal Engine type used as an attribute is silently missed, which the contract's MUST NOT calls a defect ("a position the language allows and the rule misses is a defect, not a boundary"). The same probe shows member names (`Create`→Method, `Field`→Field, `Prop`→Property, method groups) resolve through the identical registration, which is exactly what AG0041's "an internal Engine member named anywhere other than the approved call" needs. Risk-first and most-general both hand back `ISymbol`; that is required, not stylistic. Simplest's name `WrittenTypeScanner` is a misnomer for the same reason.

ORIGINAL CONTRIBUTION. Risk-first's AG0029 ruling is the highest-value output of the whole stage and I confirmed it independently against `src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:90-91`: `CrossPlatformAdapters adapters = CrossPlatformAdapters.Create();` is a genuine carried type, but `IPlatformServices platform = global::AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.PlatformServices.Create();` declares the Abstractions interface — `PlatformServices` never appears as a carried type anywhere in `Create()`. Acceptance 21 still requires AG0029 to prove the accept path "including as the declared type of a local," so the ruling (prove it with a synthetic fixture; never edit `Create()` to manufacture one, which the contract's shape-freeze forbids) forecloses two real corner-cuts, one of which would breach the contract outright. It also caught the `using static` ambiguity in the approved exemption wording and correctly refused to reinterpret it alone.

WHAT RISK-FIRST GOT WRONG, and I am rejecting: its carried-type-lens-single-owner rule ("no file other than DeclaredTypeScanner.cs calls TypeTree.Any") is factually false today — `ContractPattern.cs:50` and `ReturnTypesMustNotBeTuplesAnalyzer.cs:131` already call it — and it contradicts the contract's own reuse ledger, which directs AG0041, AG0023, and AG0029 each to pass their own leaf test into `TypeTree.Any`. It would fail the build on landing. Replaced below with a formulation that is green on landing.

risks: The new file name and its responsibilities need Tim's explicit yes before RULE-PHASE builds against them. The contract reserved exactly this ('DESIGN names that second file and brings its name and responsibilities for approval'), so WrittenNameScanner.cs is an open item until he approves that wording, not a decision this stage may record as settled.

The approved AG0041 exemption is worded as a receiver-shaped test — 'the SystemServices type named as the receiver of an invocation of its static Create method'. With `using static AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices;` a bare `Create()` resolves to the identical method symbol but has NO receiver node, so a syntax-shape-keyed exemption could misclassify it in either direction. Neither live call site uses using-static (Program.cs:62 and SystemServicesBuilder.cs:77 both write the receiver), so nothing in the acceptance set exercises it. RULE-PHASE implements the exemption on resolved symbol identity, the way PlatformFactory.Is already tests identity rather than syntax shape — and if the semantic reading would change WHAT is permitted, it stops and brings the wording to Tim rather than reinterpreting an approved exemption.

AG0029's carried-type door exemption has no production case and must never be given one. Verified against src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:86-107: Create() declares no field, property, parameter, or local of type PlatformServices — the per-OS local is declared IPlatformServices (line 91) — while CrossPlatformAdapters IS a real carried type (line 90). Acceptance 21 still requires AG0029 to prove the accept path 'including as the declared type of a local', so prove it with a synthetic fixture, exactly as every existing AG0023/AG0029 test already builds a fabricated subject compilation. Two corner-cuts are foreclosed: silently dropping AG0029's carried-type accept test because 'it never happens for real' (leaving the two rules asymmetric), and editing Create()'s body to manufacture a real occurrence (a direct breach of the contract's shape-freeze).

The AG0041 exemption must cover TWO nodes for the single approved call, not one: the SystemServices receiver node (resolves to NamedType) AND the Create node (resolves to Method). The probe confirms both fire from the one written-name registration. Exempting only the receiver leaves the approved call reported by the member half, and Acceptance 8 goes red.

The written-name lens fires on EVERY `var` whose inferred type is guarded — GetSymbolInfo on a `var` IdentifierName returns the inferred type, probe-confirmed — so it overlaps DeclaredTypeScanner on every inferred local, and both lenses fire on every ordinary declaration. This is contract-blessed ('The contract sets no required diagnostic count… no cross-lens deduplication is built'; Acceptance 11 forbids Assert.Single on an input that can trip both lenses), but TDD must compute exact expected counts per fixture rather than assume one diagnostic per statement.

Registering on IdentifierName/GenericName visits every identifier in the gated compilation, not only type positions — broader than AG0007's four narrow registrations. Bounded in practice: AG0041 gates to two small compilations (guard, AgentGuard.TestHelpers) and the AG0023/AG0029 extension to one (AgentGuard.Engine), and AG0011 already registers MemberUseScanner.Register with no gate at all across every compilation (RawPrimitiveOnlyInOwnerAnalyzer.cs:58). This is inside the existing envelope, not a new category of cost.

A name inside an XML doc-comment <see cref="..."/> is not visited — RegisterSyntaxNodeAction does not descend into structured trivia by default. This is not a gap against the contract, whose required-position lists (AG0041 and the AG0023/AG0029 extension) never name a cref, but it is stated here so it is not later mistaken for an overlooked case.

AG0007 (ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer.cs:49-52) has the identical 'enumerated syntax-kind list, next position silently escapes' gap this design fixes — but for a different type set (contract-implementation classes) and it is named nowhere in this contract's Decisions, Surfaces, or Acceptance. Migrating it onto WrittenNameScanner is a genuine improvement and out of scope: file a GitHub issue, do not fold it into this run.

Contract bookkeeping that must actually happen on approval, not just be noted: Surfaces gains WrittenNameScanner.cs beside DeclaredTypeScanner.cs, AND the reuse-ledger row currently filed under `new analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer.cs` is retargeted to the new file. Left as written, that row reads as though the written-name lens lives inside AG0041 — which the same contract forbids two paragraphs earlier ('neither may live inside AG0041').

GROUND left one RULE-PHASE item open that is adjacent to these consumers: whether SharedAnalyzerSources.cs carries one fake-AgentGuard.Engine fixture constant or two differently-shaped ones (a subject-compilation shape for the AG0040/AG0023/AG0029 Engine gates versus a reference-compilation shape for AG0041). The scanner surface is agnostic to the outcome, but the item must not get lost between this stage and RULE-PHASE.
